questions.question: What problem does the Teardown functionality help prevent in Robot Framework?

options.text: Issues when a preceding test|task fails and leaves the system in an unclean state, affecting subsequent tests|tasks
Slow execution performance due to resource allocation overhead
options.explanation: Teardowns address cleanup and state management, not performance optimization

options.text: Compilation errors when tests are executed in the wrong order
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't have compilation; teardowns address state cleanup

options.text: Memory leaks from variable declarations in test cases
options.explanation: Teardowns are for explicit cleanup actions, not automatic memory management

questions.question: What is a Teardown in Robot Framework?

options.text: A single keyword call with potential argument values that is executed after completion, regardless of outcome
A sequence of keywords that execute only when tests fail
options.explanation: Teardowns are single keyword calls and run regardless of pass/fail status

options.text: A setting that executes after the *** Variables *** section is evaluated
options.explanation: Teardowns execute after tests/tasks/suites complete, not after variable evaluation

options.text: An automatic cleanup process that runs without explicit definition
options.explanation: Teardowns must be explicitly defined; they are not automatic

questions.question: When is a Teardown executed?

options.text: After the respective scope has completed execution, regardless of the outcome
Only when the test|task or keyword fails
options.explanation: Teardowns execute regardless of success or failure

options.text: Only when the test|task or keyword passes successfully
options.explanation: Teardowns execute regardless of the outcome

options.text: Before the test|task body but after setup
options.explanation: Teardowns execute after completion, not before the body

questions.question: Which are typical use cases for Teardowns?

options.text: Cleaning up the system under test after a test|task has been executed
Closing connections to databases, files, or other resources
Resetting the system under test to a known state
Closing user sessions or logging out users
Initializing test data before test execution
options.explanation: Data initialization is a Setup task, not a Teardown task

questions.question: What status do not-executed keywords receive when a keyword with status FAIL causes Robot Framework to stop executing subsequent keywords?

options.text: NOT RUN
SKIPPED
options.explanation: The status is NOT RUN, not SKIPPED

options.text: PENDING
options.explanation: There is no PENDING status; not-executed keywords are marked NOT RUN

options.text: FAIL
options.explanation: NOT RUN status is different from FAIL; these keywords weren't attempted

questions.question: When is a Suite Teardown executed?

options.text: After all tests|tasks and all child suites in a suite have been executed
After each test|task in the suite individually
options.explanation: This describes Test Teardown, not Suite Teardown

options.text: Before child suites but after all tests|tasks in the parent suite
options.explanation: Suite Teardown runs after both tests and child suites complete

options.text: Only if all tests|tasks in the suite passed
options.explanation: Suite Teardown runs regardless of test outcomes

questions.question: Does Suite Teardown execute if the Suite Setup fails?

options.text: Yes, Suite Teardown executes even if Suite Setup fails
No, if Setup fails, Teardown is skipped
options.explanation: Teardown always runs regardless of Setup status

options.text: Yes, but only if at least one test was attempted
options.explanation: Suite Teardown runs even if no tests were executed due to Setup failure

options.text: No, Suite Teardown requires successful Setup execution
options.explanation: Teardown runs regardless of Setup success or failure

questions.question: What happens if a Suite Teardown fails?

options.text: All tests|tasks in the suite are marked as failed in reports and logs
Only the Suite Teardown itself is marked as failed; test results are unaffected
options.explanation: Suite Teardown failure causes all tests in the suite to be marked as failed

options.text: The suite is retried once before marking tests as failed
options.explanation: There is no automatic retry mechanism for Suite Teardown

options.text: Only tests that passed are marked as failed; already-failed tests remain failed
options.explanation: All tests in the suite are marked as failed when Suite Teardown fails

questions.question: What happens when a keyword within a Suite Teardown fails?

options.text: All keywords within the Suite Teardown are still executed, even if one fails
Execution of the Suite Teardown stops at the failed keyword
options.explanation: Teardowns continue executing all keywords even when some fail

options.text: The failed keyword is retried once before continuing
options.explanation: There is no automatic retry in teardowns

options.text: Only remaining keywords without dependencies on the failed keyword execute
options.explanation: All keywords in the teardown execute regardless of failures

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Teardown    Close All Resources    force=True
```

What does this Suite Teardown do?

options.text: Calls 'Close All Resources' keyword with named argument force=True after all tests and child suites complete
Calls 'Close All Resources' after each test with the force parameter
options.explanation: Suite Teardown runs once after all tests, not after each test

options.text: Forces all resources to close even if Setup fails
options.explanation: While it does run even if Setup fails, 'force=True' is an argument to the keyword, not a Suite Teardown setting

options.text: Defines a variable ${force} with value True for use in teardown
options.explanation: This is a keyword call with an argument, not a variable definition

questions.question: When is a Test|Task Teardown executed?

options.text: After a single test|task body has been executed
After all tests|tasks in the suite have been executed
options.explanation: This describes Suite Teardown, not Test|Task Teardown

options.text: Before the test|task body but after setup
options.explanation: Teardown runs after the test body, not before

options.text: Only after successful test|task execution
options.explanation: Test|Task Teardown runs regardless of test success or failure

questions.question: Does Test|Task Teardown execute if the Test|Task Setup fails?

options.text: Yes, Test|Task Teardown executes even if Test|Task Setup fails
No, Teardown requires successful Setup execution
options.explanation: Teardown always runs regardless of Setup status

options.text: Yes, but only if at least one keyword in the test body was executed
options.explanation: Teardown runs even if the test body wasn't executed due to Setup failure

options.text: No, if Setup fails, the entire test including Teardown is skipped
options.explanation: The test body is skipped but Teardown still runs

questions.question: Where can you define a default Test|Task Teardown that applies to all tests|tasks in a suite?

options.text: In the *** Settings *** section using the Test Teardown or Task Teardown setting
In the *** Variables *** section as ${TEST_TEARDOWN}
options.explanation: Test Teardown is a setting, not a variable

options.text: In each test|task using the [Teardown] tag
options.explanation: [Teardown] is for individual test overrides, not default settings

options.text: In a separate teardown.robot resource file
options.explanation: Default Test Teardown is defined in the suite's *** Settings *** section

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Test Teardown    Logout User

*** Test Cases ***
Custom Teardown Test
    Perform Test Steps
    [Teardown]    Cleanup Specific Data
```

What teardown will be executed for 'Custom Teardown Test'?

options.text: Cleanup Specific Data (the local [Teardown] overrides the default)
Both Logout User and Cleanup Specific Data (both are executed)
options.explanation: Local [Teardown] completely overrides the default

options.text: Logout User (default Test Teardown always applies)
options.explanation: Local [Teardown] overrides the default Test Teardown

options.text: No teardown (the [Teardown] tag disables teardown)
options.explanation: [Teardown] with a keyword name calls that keyword; only [Teardown] NONE disables teardown

questions.question: How do you disable a Test|Task Teardown for a specific test|task?

options.text: Use [Teardown] NONE in the test|task
Use [Teardown] ${EMPTY} in the test|task
options.explanation: NONE is the specific keyword to disable teardown, not ${EMPTY}

options.text: Omit the [Teardown] setting from the test|task
options.explanation: Omitting [Teardown] means the default Test Teardown will be used if defined

options.text: Use [Disable Teardown] in the test|task
options.explanation: There is no [Disable Teardown] setting; use [Teardown] NONE

questions.question: Is NONE case-sensitive when used to disable teardowns?

options.text: Yes, NONE must be in uppercase
No, none, None, or NONE all work the same way
options.explanation: NONE is case-sensitive and must be uppercase

options.text: Yes, but only for Test Teardown, not other teardown types
options.explanation: NONE is case-sensitive for all teardown types

options.text: No, Robot Framework is case-insensitive for all keywords and settings
options.explanation: While keywords are generally case-insensitive, NONE is a special case-sensitive value

questions.question: Where is it recommended to place the local [Teardown] setting in a test|task?

options.text: As the last line of the test|task
As the first line of the test|task, immediately after the test name
options.explanation: While functional, it's recommended to place it as the last line for readability

options.text: Immediately before the keyword that might fail
options.explanation: Teardown is a test-level setting, not placed before specific keywords

options.text: In the *** Settings *** section, not in the test|task body
options.explanation: Local overrides use [Teardown] in the test body; *** Settings *** is for defaults

questions.question: What happens if a Test|Task Teardown fails?

options.text: The test|task is marked as failed in reports and logs
The test|task result remains as it was (pass/fail); only teardown is marked as failed
options.explanation: Teardown failure causes the entire test to be marked as failed

options.text: All remaining tests in the suite are also marked as failed
options.explanation: Only the current test is affected; other tests continue (unlike Suite Teardown)

options.text: The teardown is automatically retried once
options.explanation: There is no automatic retry mechanism for teardowns

questions.question: Which are typical use cases for Test|Task Teardown?

options.text: Logging out of an application after a test|task completes
Deleting test data created during the test|task
Restoring configurations altered during the test|task
Distinguishing phases of a test|task (setup, steps, teardown)
Closing services needed by all tests in the suite
options.explanation: Suite-wide service closure should be in Suite Teardown, not Test Teardown

questions.question: When is a Keyword Teardown executed?

options.text: After a user keyword body has been executed
After any test that calls the keyword
options.explanation: Keyword Teardown runs when that specific keyword completes, not at test end

options.text: Before the keyword's return statement
options.explanation: Teardown runs after the keyword body, including any return

options.text: Only the last time the keyword is called in a suite
options.explanation: Keyword Teardown runs every time the keyword is called

questions.question: Does Keyword Teardown execute if the keyword's setup fails?

options.text: Yes, Keyword Teardown executes even if the keyword's setup fails
No, Teardown requires successful Setup execution
options.explanation: Teardown always runs regardless of Setup status

options.text: Yes, but only if at least one keyword in the body was executed
options.explanation: Teardown runs even if the body wasn't executed due to Setup failure

options.text: No, if Setup fails, the entire keyword including Teardown is skipped
options.explanation: The keyword body is skipped but Teardown still runs

questions.question:
```robot
*** Keywords ***
Process Data
    Open Data Connection
    Process the Data
    [Teardown]    Close Data Connection
```

Where is it recommended to place the [Teardown] setting for readability?

options.text: As the last line of the keyword (as shown in the example)
As the first line after the keyword name
options.explanation: While functional, it's recommended as the last line for better readability

options.text: Immediately after the [Setup] setting
options.explanation: Setup and Teardown are typically separated by the keyword body

options.text: In the *** Settings *** section of the suite
options.explanation: Keyword Teardown is defined within the keyword, not in suite settings

questions.question: What happens when a keyword within a Keyword Teardown fails?

options.text: All keywords within the Keyword Teardown are still executed, even if one fails
Execution of the Keyword Teardown stops at the failed keyword
options.explanation: Teardowns continue executing all keywords even when some fail

options.text: The failed keyword is retried before continuing
options.explanation: There is no automatic retry mechanism

options.text: Only critical keywords continue executing
options.explanation: All keywords in the teardown execute regardless of failures

questions.question: Which are typical use cases for Keyword Teardown?

options.text: Closing temporary files or connections opened within the keyword
Resetting variables or states altered during keyword execution
Logging additional information after keyword execution
Cleaning up the entire test environment after all tests complete
options.explanation: Environment cleanup after all tests is a Suite Teardown use case

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup     Initialize Database
Suite Teardown  Cleanup Database
Test Teardown   Reset Session

*** Test Cases ***
Test One
    Perform Database Query

Test Two
    [Teardown]    NONE
    Perform Another Query
```

Which teardowns execute for 'Test Two'?

options.text: Only Suite Teardown (after all tests complete)
Both Reset Session and Cleanup Database
options.explanation: [Teardown] NONE disables the Test Teardown; only Suite Teardown runs

options.text: None, [Teardown] NONE disables all teardowns
options.explanation: [Teardown] NONE only disables the test-level teardown, not Suite Teardown

options.text: Reset Session, because default Test Teardown cannot be overridden
options.explanation: [Teardown] NONE overrides and disables the default Test Teardown

questions.question:
```robot
*** Keywords ***
Database Operation
    [Setup]    Connect To Database
    Execute Query    ${SQL}
    [Teardown]    Disconnect From Database
```

If 'Connect To Database' fails, what executes?

options.text: Only 'Disconnect From Database' (Teardown runs even when Setup fails)
Nothing executes because Setup failed
options.explanation: Teardown runs even when Setup fails

options.text: Only 'Execute Query' and 'Disconnect From Database'
options.explanation: When Setup fails, the keyword body doesn't execute, but Teardown does

options.text: All three keywords execute in sequence regardless of failures
options.explanation: Setup failure prevents body execution; only Teardown runs

questions.question: What is the key benefit of Teardowns always executing regardless of outcome?

options.text: Ensures clean state for subsequent tests, reducing inter-test dependencies
Improves speed by parallelizing cleanup across test execution
options.explanation: Teardowns address reliability through cleanup, not performance

options.text: Allows failed tests to pass by cleaning up error conditions
options.explanation: Teardowns don't change test results; they ensure cleanup

options.text: Prevents error messages from appearing in test reports
options.explanation: Teardowns still log errors; benefit is guaranteed cleanup

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Test Teardown    Logout User

*** Test Cases ***
Test With Default
    Login User
    Do Testing

No Teardown Test
    Perform Steps
    [Teardown]    NONE

Custom Teardown
    Do More Testing
    [Teardown]    Special Cleanup
```

Which tests execute 'Logout User'?

options.text: Only 'Test With Default'
'Test With Default' and 'Custom Teardown'
options.explanation: 'Custom Teardown' has its own teardown that overrides the default

options.text: All three tests (default applies to all)
options.explanation: 'No Teardown Test' uses NONE and 'Custom Teardown' has a different teardown

options.text: None, because [Teardown] declarations disable the default
options.explanation: Only 'Test With Default' has no [Teardown] declaration, so it uses the default

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Suite Setup     Start Services
Suite Teardown  Stop Services

*** Test Cases ***
Test One
    Keyword A    # Fails
    Keyword B    # NOT RUN
    Keyword C    # NOT RUN
```

What is the status of 'Stop Services' when Keyword A fails?

options.text: It executes normally regardless of Keyword A's failure
It receives status NOT RUN because a keyword in the test failed
options.explanation: Suite Teardown always executes regardless of test failures

options.text: It executes with a modified cleanup-only mode
options.explanation: Teardown executes normally; there is no special mode

options.text: It only executes if there are more tests after Test One
options.explanation: Suite Teardown executes after all tests regardless of how many tests there are

questions.question:
```robot
*** Keywords ***
Multi-Step Cleanup
    Close Application    # Fails
    Delete Temp Files    # Executes anyway
    Reset Config         # Executes anyway
```

If this is used as a Suite Teardown and 'Close Application' fails, what happens?

options.text: All three keywords execute, and all tests in the suite are marked as failed
Execution stops at 'Close Application' and tests remain with their original status
options.explanation: All teardown keywords execute even when some fail, and Suite Teardown failure marks all tests as failed

options.text: Only 'Delete Temp Files' and 'Reset Config' execute; tests keep original status
options.explanation: All three execute, but Suite Teardown failure marks all tests as failed

options.text: All three execute with a warning, but test results are not affected
options.explanation: Suite Teardown failure causes all tests to be marked as failed
